Z_sector_diagnostic_limitation.source_explanation: TRACE delivered_bytes uses persistent request.credited across calls, while delivered_sectors uses a diag.sectors_read value sampled at current GD entry. IRQ credits between GD entries can be omitted from the sector diagnostic. This is not evidence of 35 missing payload sectors.

Z delivered-sectors diagnostic is 4,356 while requested sectors and both byte counters correspond to 4,391. Source inspection explains an asynchronous observation gap: TRACE adds bytes since the preceding observed request credit, but sectors only since the current GD-call entry. SCI IRQ progress between GD calls can therefore increase bytes without the corresponding TRACE sector delta. This 35-sector mismatch is not evidence of missing payload bytes; the precise IRQ contribution was not reconstructed.

purpose: Hardware comparison of delivered B/Y/Z DATA scheduling candidates

facts: Z admits up to four verified physical 512-byte blocks per foreground interval, with a 1500-tick (1.92ms) time allowance checked between steps.
Two raw 2352-byte image sectors need about 10–11 physical blocks depending on alignment; four blocks are less than one raw sector.
Only 142 of 20260 verified Z blocks (0.700888%) were processed in IRQ context.
Z mean pending-service gap was about 5.097ms; the matched 480-sector request took about2.35 times as long as B.
source_based_hypothesis.inference: The foreground allowance may be too small for the observed game call cadence, while scarce IRQ progress fails to make up the difference.
source_based_hypothesis.limits: Service gaps include game/potential IRQ work outside observed GD bodies. The report does not prove the allowance caused them, and aggregate IRQ share is not per-request evidence.
